transcript.text: Hi. I'm Sal, a helper on this tablet. I'm not a person, and a staff member will check everything with you. I'll ask a few short questions and take short notes for your case manager. You can skip any of them. What's on your mind most right now?
They say I'm done here Friday. I can't go back under the bridge with this leg. Where do I go?
Friday, and you can't go back under the bridge with that leg. That's a hard spot. I'll pass that to your case manager. Do you have a way to get around, like a walker, or do stairs give you trouble?
Yeah, I use a walker, and stairs are a real problem for me. I need something on the ground floor, or a bottom bunk if it's a shelter.
Got it. A walker, and a ground floor or bottom bunk. That helps a lot. Do you have an ID card or any papers with your name on them?
No, I lost my ID a while back. I've got my Medi-Cal card, though, and I think that's still good.
Okay, you have your Medi-Cal card, and you lost your ID. Thanks for telling me. What city were you living in before you came here?
Santa Ana, mostly. I was around there for a long time before things fell apart.
Santa Ana, for a long time. Got it. Are you a veteran, meaning you ever served in the military?
I don't think so, no. Nobody's ever asked me that in a way that made me sure, but I never signed up for anything like that.
Okay, you never signed up for the military, so I'll note that. How old are you, roughly? A range is fine, like your 40s or over 60.
Sixty-two. Turned sixty-two not long ago.
Sixty-two. Thanks for telling me. What kind of phone do you have, a smartphone, a flip phone, or none right now?
Just a basic phone. It makes calls and I can send texts, but that's about it. No internet or apps.

Here's what I heard: You're leaving recuperative care on Friday. You use a walker, so you need a ground floor spot or a bottom bunk. You lost your ID, but you have your Medi-Cal card. You lived in Santa Ana for a long time. You don't think you've served in the military. You're sixty-two. You have a basic phone that makes calls and texts. Did I get that right?
Yes, that's right.
Thank you. I'll pass this to your case manager, and I'll look into your next step now.

transcript.text: Hola. Soy Sal. Estoy en esta tableta para ayudarte. No soy una persona, y alguien del equipo va a revisar todo contigo. Te voy a hacer unas preguntas cortas y tomar notas breves para tu administrador de caso. Puedes saltar cualquiera. ¿Qué es lo que más necesitas ahora?
Yo sé trabajar. Solo necesito como dos mil dólares para el equipo y el permiso.
Entiendo, usted sabe trabajar y necesita unos dos mil dólares para el equipo y el permiso. ¿Qué tipo de trabajo hace o quiere hacer?
Quiero volver a vender comida, como antes en los swap meets. Tengo experiencia con tamales y aguas frescas, y ya sé cómo hacer las cuentas para que me rinda.
Tamales y aguas frescas, qué bueno, usted ya sabe el oficio. ¿Tiene una cuenta de banco y algún tipo de identificación, como una licencia o una tarjeta del estado?
No tengo cuenta de banco ahorita. Y sobre los papeles de identificación, prefiero no hablar de eso, eso es privado para mí.
Está bien, no tiene que hablar de eso. Lo anoto y no le voy a preguntar más sobre papeles. Sin cuenta de banco, ¿tiene ya algún permiso o registro para su negocio de comida?
No, todavía no tengo nada de eso. Por eso necesito que me digan bien los pasos, porque no sé por dónde empezar con el permiso de comida del condado.
Entiendo, usted no sabe por dónde empezar con el permiso. Eso lo vemos después, cuando tengamos la lista. Una pregunta más: ¿cuándo sale de aquí, y a dónde piensa ir?

Pues, todavía no sé bien. Por ahorita estoy en un lugar donde me dejan quedarme unos días, pero no quiero dar la dirección ni el nombre del lugar. Lo que sí quiero es encontrar un espacio en algún swap meet del condado de Orange para vender los fines de semana.
Entiendo, no tiene que dar la dirección ni el nombre del lugar. Usted quiere vender los fines de semana en un swap meet del condado de Orange. ¿Hay algún lugar donde pueda recibir correo o llamadas?
Pues, no tengo dirección fija para correo. Pero tengo mi teléfono con datos, así que me pueden llamar o mandar mensaje ahí, y yo reviso seguido.
Gracias, ya tengo su teléfono con datos y que lo revisa seguido. Ahora, ¿cuántos años tiene más o menos? Puede decir un rango, como en sus 40.
Tengo 41 años, o sea, en mis 40. Pero le digo algo: ya llevo bastante tiempo tratando de levantarme, y lo que más necesito es que alguien me ayude con los pasos del permiso sin tanto papeleo confuso.

Esto es lo que escuché: quiere vender tamales y aguas frescas en un swap meet del condado de Orange los fines de semana. Necesita unos dos mil dólares para el equipo y el permiso, y ayuda con los pasos sin papeleo confuso. No tiene cuenta de banco ni permiso todavía. Recibe mensajes en su teléfono con datos. Tiene 41 años. ¿Esto es lo que quiere? ¿Lo entendí bien?
Sí, así es. Lo entendió bien. Solo que lo de los dos mil dólares es para el equipo y el permiso, y también necesito que alguien me explique bien los pasos.
Gracias, ya anoté que el dinero es para el equipo y el permiso, y que necesita que le expliquen los pasos. Ahora vamos a buscar su siguiente paso.

entry.cost: 8.99% – 14.99% fixed, simple interest; no application fees; closing costs financed into the loan

options.reason: Zero-interest business loans exist, but permanent residence, proof of income and a valid CA ID are required; client has no fixed address and prefers not to discuss ID.

transcript.text: Hi. I'm Sal, a helper on this tablet. I'm not a person, and a staff member will check everything with you. I'll ask a few short questions and take short notes for your case manager. You can skip any of them. What's on your mind most right now?
I don't hear well on the phone. Is there somebody I can go see?

I'm sorry, that's hard. I can't find a place to see someone yet, but I'll pass that to your case manager, and they can help you with it. Would you like to tell me a little more so I can pass it along, or would you rather stop here?
Maybe a little more. I'd rather come in person or get things written down, if that's possible. I take the bus, so somewhere close to a stop would help.
Got it. You'd like things in person or written down, and you take the bus, so a spot near a stop helps. What do you need most when you leave here: a place to sleep, work, or getting home to family?
Honestly, I need help with money and food right now. I don't have any income, and I'm not sure what I qualify for. Is there a place I could go in person to find that out?
I hear you. Money and food come first right now. I can't tell you where to go yet, but I'll pass it to your case manager. Do you have a phone, or do you get phone calls?
Yes, I have a phone, but calls are hard for me. Texting is much easier, if you can reach me that way.
Texting is easier, so I'll note that. Got it. What's the last city you lived in?
I've been in Santa Ana for a long time, right here in Orange County. Why do you need to know that?
Fair question. It helps us know which local places to check for you. Santa Ana, got it. Do you have an ID card or any papers with your name on them right now?
I have my California ID card, and I think my Social Security card is in my folder at home. I'm not sure where my other papers are.
Thanks, that helps. You have a California ID, and your Social Security card is at home in a folder. Do you know roughly how old you are? A range is fine, like 50s or over 60.
Sixty-seven. I'll be sixty-eight in the spring, if that matters.

Yes, that's right. I'd add that I'm not sure what I qualify for, so that's the main thing I need help figuring out.

I never asked them for anything. Don't know if I even count.
You count. You don't have to ask for anything yet. We can just talk about what's coming up when you leave. Is there one thing that worries you most about leaving here?
Honestly, I don't have a place to go yet. My sister's couch is the plan, and I don't know how long that works.
Got it. A place to sleep, and your sister's couch for now. Is that a place you'd be able to stay for a while, or more of a short-term plan?
Right now it's short-term. She said a few weeks, maybe a month, but I don't want to wear out my welcome. She's got her own stuff going on.

That helps, thank you. A few weeks at your sister's is a real plan, and you're thinking ahead about not wearing out your welcome. Do you have any ID with you right now, like a driver's license or state ID?
I've got a driver's license, yeah. It's in my wallet, or it was last time I checked. I don't have my discharge papers, though, and I don't even know where those would be.
Okay, you have your driver's license, and you're not sure where your discharge papers are. That's fine. Can you tell me how you get around, like walking, stairs, or a walker?
Walking's fine for me. Bad knee sometimes, especially on stairs, but I don't use a walker or anything like that.
Okay, you walk fine, but your knee bothers you on stairs. Thanks for telling me. What was the last city you lived in before you came here?
Anaheim, mostly. I was in a rented room there for a couple years before things fell apart.
Anaheim, got it. A rented room for a couple years. Is your sister's place in Orange County too, or somewhere else?
Yeah, she's in Orange County too, over in Garden Grove. It's close enough that I can get there on the bus.

Here's what I heard: you're leaving to your sister's couch in Garden Grove for a few weeks, maybe a month. You have your driver's license, but not your discharge papers. You walk fine, but your knee bothers you on stairs. Your last city was Anaheim. You can get to her place by bus. Did I get that right?
Yeah, that's right. Couch in Garden Grove, a few weeks, maybe a month. Driver's license, no discharge papers. Knee's a problem on stairs. Anaheim before this, and the bus gets me there.
Thanks, that's everything I need for now. I'll pass this to your case manager, and we'll look at your next step now. You can still ask them anything about it.
